aaron.name: Aaron
aaron.role: Brother of Moses; the lesser priesthood bears his name
aaron.dateNote: Section 84, dated 22–23 September 1832, gives the fullest account of him in the D&C.
aaron.importance: Section 84 says the Lord confirmed a priesthood on Aaron and his seed. It says this lesser priesthood continued with “the house of Aaron” until John the Baptist. Teachers and deacons are called appendages of that priesthood. The revelation speaks of faithful members becoming “the sons of Moses and of Aaron.”
aaron.connections: The D&C presents him as Moses’s brother and companion. Section 28 compares Oliver Cowdery’s role to Aaron’s beside Moses.

sources.title: Doctrine and Covenants 84 (official text)

abraham.name: Abraham
abraham.role: Biblical patriarch and father of the covenant
abraham.dateNote: Section 84 says he received the priesthood from Melchizedek.
abraham.importance: Section 84 places him in the priesthood line and says the faithful become “the seed of Abraham.” In section 110 Elias commits “the gospel of Abraham.” Section 132 says Abraham received wives and concubines by command and was not condemned, and it tells Joseph Smith to “do the works of Abraham.” Sections 137 and 138 report seeing him among the saved.
abraham.connections: The D&C names Melchizedek, Isaac, Jacob, Sarah, and Hagar with him. Section 124 says Joseph Smith Sr. “sitteth with Abraham.”

sources.title: Doctrine and Covenants 84
Doctrine and Covenants 110
Doctrine and Covenants 27

adam.name: Adam
adam.role: First man, called Michael and the Ancient of Days
adam.dateNote: The D&C says he blessed his posterity at Adam-ondi-Ahman three years before his death.
adam.importance: Section 27 names him “Michael, or Adam, the father of all.” Section 29 recounts his temptation and fall and says God gave him and his seed time to repent. Section 107 says the priesthood order began in his day and lists the patriarchs he ordained. It also tells of his final blessing at Adam-ondi-Ahman, and section 116 says he will return there.
adam.connections: The D&C names his sons Abel and Seth and his descendant Enoch. In sections 137 and 138 Joseph Smith and Joseph F. Smith report seeing “Father Adam.”

sources.title: Doctrine and Covenants 27
Doctrine and Covenants 107

almon-babbitt.name: Almon W. Babbitt
almon-babbitt.role: Church agent and lawyer rebuked in section 124
almon-babbitt.dateNote: He was appointed president of the Kirtland stake in October 1840; section 124 rebukes him in January 1841.
almon-babbitt.importance: Section 124 says he set up his own counsel instead of the First Presidency’s and compares this to a golden calf. Historians link this to his urging Saints to stay at Kirtland rather than gather to Nauvoo. He was restored and later led at Ramus and served as a Church trustee in 1846. He was disciplined several times, excommunicated in 1854, and killed on the plains in 1856.
almon-babbitt.connections: He married Julia Ann Johnson in 1833. He worked under Joseph Smith and later Brigham Young, and became secretary of Utah Territory in 1852.

sources.title: Almon Whiting Babbitt, Joseph Smith Papers biography
Almon W. Babbitt, Wikipedia

alvin-smith.name: Alvin Smith
alvin-smith.dateNote: He died on 19 November 1823, years before the Church was organized; section 137 is dated 21 January 1836.
alvin-smith.importance: Alvin Smith was the eldest son of the Smith family; he worked to pay for their farm and oversaw building their Manchester home. He died in 1823 after a severe stomach illness, before the Church existed. In section 137 Joseph reports seeing Alvin in the celestial kingdom and wondering how, since Alvin was never baptized. The revelation answers that those who would have received the gospel will be heirs of that kingdom.
alvin-smith.connections: He was the son of Joseph Smith Sr. and Lucy Mack Smith and older brother of Hyrum and Joseph Smith.

sources.title: Alvin Smith, Joseph Smith Papers biography

amasa-lyman.name: Amasa Lyman
amasa-lyman.role: Apostle who helped lead the 1847 westward companies
amasa-lyman.dateNote: He became an apostle on 20 August 1842; section 136 names him in January 1847.
amasa-lyman.importance: Section 124 names him a counselor in the presidency of the high priests at Nauvoo. Section 136 tells him and George A. Smith to organize a company for the journey west. He led wagon companies to the Salt Lake Valley in 1847–1848. He lost his apostleship in 1867 and was excommunicated in 1870.
amasa-lyman.connections: Lyman E. Johnson baptized him in 1832. In section 136 he works with George A. Smith.

sources.title: Amasa Mason Lyman, Joseph Smith Papers biography

amos-davies.name: Amos Davies
amos-davies.role: Commerce merchant told to invest in the Nauvoo House
amos-davies.dateNote: He was baptized in April 1840; section 124 names him in January 1841.
amos-davies.importance: He was a merchant and postmaster at Commerce before the Saints arrived. Section 124 tells him to pay stock to those building the Nauvoo House. It says he must also obey Joseph Smith’s counsel and be humble. In 1842–1843 the city of Nauvoo brought several cases against him, including slander of Joseph Smith.
amos-davies.connections: He dealt with Joseph Smith and the Nauvoo House committee of George Miller, Lyman Wight, John Snider, and Peter Haws.

sources.title: Amos Davis, Joseph Smith Papers biography

asa-dodds.name: Asa Dodds
asa-dodds.role: Early elder sent to the western countries
asa-dodds.dateNote: He was an elder by February 1831; section 75 names him in January 1832.
asa-dodds.importance: In 1831 he travelled with Orson Pratt from Missouri to Indiana. Section 75 sends him and Calves Wilson to preach in the western countries. Little else is known; by 1835 he had moved to Tennessee.
asa-dodds.connections: His companion in section 75 was Calves Wilson.

sources.title: Asa Dodds, Joseph Smith Papers biography

brigham-young.name: Brigham Young
brigham-young.role: President of the Twelve and later President of the Church
brigham-young.dateNote: He was baptized in April 1832, ordained an apostle on 14 February 1835, and gave section 136 on 14 January 1847.
brigham-young.importance: He later gave the account linking section 89 to tobacco use at the school of the prophets. Section 124 names him president of the Twelve in 1841. Section 126, given at his Nauvoo home after his mission to England, releases him from leaving his family again. After Joseph Smith’s death he led the Church, and section 136 is the revelation he gave at Winter Quarters for the trek west.
brigham-young.connections: Husband of Mary Ann Angell Young, named in the setting of section 126. He served with Heber C. Kimball and the other apostles, and Joseph F. Smith saw him among the spirits in section 138.

sources.title: Brigham Young, Joseph Smith Papers

burr-riggs.name: Burr Riggs
burr-riggs.dateNote: He was ordained a high priest on 25 October 1831; section 75 sends him south in January 1832.
burr-riggs.importance: Section 75 sends him with Major N. Ashley to preach in the south. He was excommunicated in 1833 and later reinstated. He marched with the Camp of Israel in 1834 and later settled in Quincy, Illinois.
burr-riggs.connections: His companion in section 75 was Major N. Ashley.

sources.title: Burr Riggs, Joseph Smith Papers biography

calves-wilson.name: Calves Wilson
calves-wilson.role: Early priest sent to preach in the West
calves-wilson.dateNote: Section 75 called him to preach on 25 January 1832 at Amherst, Ohio.
calves-wilson.importance: Section 75 pairs him with Asa Dodds and sends them to preach in the “western countries.” Little else is known of him. One modern biography says he was baptized and ordained a priest in October 1831. It suggests he may have gone with Lyman Wight to Cincinnati in 1832, but that is not documented.
calves-wilson.connections: Called with Asa Dodds at the Amherst conference.

sources.title: Calves Wilson, Doctrine and Covenants Central

daniel-stanton.name: Daniel Stanton
daniel-stanton.role: Early Ohio elder and Missouri leader
daniel-stanton.dateNote: He was baptized on 3 November 1830; section 75 names him in January 1832.
daniel-stanton.importance: Section 75 pairs him with Seymour Brunson for a mission. He moved to Jackson County in 1832 and helped lead a branch in Independence. He later served on high councils in Missouri and Illinois and settled in the West.
daniel-stanton.connections: His companion in section 75 was Seymour Brunson.

sources.title: Daniel Stanton, Joseph Smith Papers biography
Daniel Stanton, Church History Biographical Database

david-w-patten.name: David W. Patten
david-w-patten.dateNote: He became an apostle on 15 February 1835 and died on 25 October 1838 after the Crooked River skirmish.
david-w-patten.importance: Section 114 tells him in April 1838 to settle his business and prepare for a mission with the Twelve the next spring. He was mortally wounded at Crooked River before that mission began. Section 124 says the Lord has taken him and that another may be appointed to his calling.
david-w-patten.connections: His brother John Patten baptized him in 1832, and he married Phoebe Ann Babcock. He served in the Twelve with Thomas B. Marsh and Brigham Young.

sources.title: David Wyman Patten, Joseph Smith Papers biography

david-whitmer.name: David Whitmer
david-whitmer.role: One of the Three Witnesses of the Book of Mormon
david-whitmer.dateNote: He was baptized in June 1829, and the revelations to him in sections 14 and 18 date from that month.
david-whitmer.importance: In June 1829 David Whitmer moved Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery from Harmony to his father’s farm in Fayette. Section 14 calls him “to assist,” and section 18 tells him and Oliver to search out the Twelve. He became one of the Three Witnesses; section 30 rebukes him for fearing man, and section 52 sends him to Missouri. He later led the Church in Missouri, was excommunicated in 1838, and kept affirming his witness.
david-whitmer.connections: He was a son of Peter Whitmer Sr.; his brothers John, Peter Jr., and Christian also joined, and his sister Elizabeth married Oliver Cowdery. Section 52 pairs him with Harvey Whitlock.

sources.title: David Whitmer, Joseph Smith Papers biography

don-carlos-smith.name: Don Carlos Smith
don-carlos-smith.role: Youngest brother of Joseph Smith and Nauvoo editor
don-carlos-smith.dateNote: He was named president of the high priests in section 124 in January 1841 and died that August.
don-carlos-smith.importance: Section 124 names him “Don C. Smith” as president over a quorum of high priests, with Amasa Lyman and Noah Packard as counselors. He had first been chosen to lead the high priests in Kirtland in 1836. He also edited the Church newspaper Times and Seasons from 1839. He died of pneumonia at Nauvoo on 7 August 1841, aged twenty-five.
don-carlos-smith.connections: Son of Joseph Smith Sr. and Lucy Mack Smith and youngest brother of Joseph and Hyrum. His daughter Ina Coolbrith became a California poet.

sources.title: Don Carlos Smith, Wikipedia

eden-smith.name: Eden Smith
eden-smith.dateNote: He was baptized in 1831; section 75 names him in January 1832 and section 80 in March 1832.
eden-smith.importance: Section 75 pairs him with Micah B. Welton. Section 80 then names him as Stephen Burnett’s companion, though illness delayed their preaching. He was disfellowshipped in 1833 and rebaptized in 1834.
eden-smith.connections: His father was a John Smith, not Joseph Smith’s uncle of that name. His named companions are Micah B. Welton and Stephen Burnett.

sources.title: Eden Smith, Doctrine and Covenants Central

edward-partridge.name: Edward Partridge
edward-partridge.dateNote: He was baptized on 11 December 1830, named bishop in February 1831, and tarred and feathered in Independence in July 1833.
edward-partridge.importance: Section 36 calls him to preach after his baptism in December 1830. Section 41 names him the first bishop, and section 42 gives the bishop his duties under the law of consecration. In Missouri he divided inheritances in Zion (57–58), though the revelations also call him to repent of disagreements with Joseph Smith. Joseph Smith addressed the Liberty Jail letters (121–123) to him and the Church.
edward-partridge.connections: He married Lydia Clisbee and had lived in Painesville, Ohio, near Sidney Rigdon’s congregation. He worked alongside Sidney Gilbert and Newel K. Whitney, and section 124 counts him among the faithful dead.

sources.title: Edward Partridge, Joseph Smith Papers biography

elias-higbee.name: Elias Higbee
elias-higbee.role: Missouri judge, high councilor, and temple committee member
elias-higbee.dateNote: He asked the questions on Isaiah 52 answered at Far West in March 1838.
elias-higbee.importance: Section 113 records his questions about Isaiah 52, on putting on strength and loosing the bands of Zion’s neck. He was a Caldwell County judge and a member of the Far West high council. In 1839–1840 he went with Joseph Smith to Washington, D.C., to seek redress for Missouri losses. He was later appointed to the Nauvoo temple building committee.
elias-higbee.connections: He traveled with Joseph Smith to Washington, D.C., and worked with the Far West and Nauvoo Church leaders.

sources.title: Elias Higbee, Joseph Smith Papers

elias.name: Elias
elias.role: Heavenly messenger named in several revelations
elias.dateNote: Section 110 says Elias appeared to Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery in the Kirtland Temple on 3 April 1836.
elias.importance: Section 27 says Elias holds the keys to restore all things and visited Zacharias, father of John the Baptist. Section 77 uses the name for one sent to gather Israel and restore all things. Section 110 says Elias appeared in the Kirtland Temple and committed “the dispensation of the gospel of Abraham.” Section 138 names an Elias who was with Moses on the Mount of Transfiguration.
elias.connections: The revelations list him with Moroni, Elijah, Moses, and John the Baptist. The D&C does not say plainly whether every use of the name means the same person.

sources.title: Doctrine and Covenants 27 (official text)
Doctrine and Covenants 110 (official text and heading)

elijah.name: Elijah
elijah.role: Old Testament prophet who restored sealing keys
elijah.dateNote: The D&C reports his appearance in the Kirtland temple on 3 April 1836.
elijah.importance: Section 2 quotes a promise that the Lord will reveal the priesthood by Elijah’s hand before the day of the Lord. Section 27 says he holds keys to turn the hearts of fathers and children to each other. In section 110 Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery report that Elijah appeared and committed those keys. Section 128 ties his mission to baptism for the dead, and section 138 repeats Malachi’s promise.
elijah.connections: The D&C sets him beside Moses and Elias in section 110 and quotes Malachi about him. The messenger in section 2 is identified as Moroni.

sources.title: Doctrine and Covenants 110
Doctrine and Covenants 27

emer-harris.name: Emer Harris
emer-harris.role: Early elder and older brother of Martin Harris
emer-harris.dateNote: He was baptized on 10 February 1831, and section 75 named him for a mission on 25 January 1832.
emer-harris.importance: Emer Harris grew up near Palmyra and was baptized in Pennsylvania in February 1831. In October 1831 he was ordained a high priest and served briefly as a scribe to Joseph Smith. Section 75 unites him in the ministry with Simeon Carter. He worked on the Kirtland and Nauvoo temples, moved to Utah, and was ordained a patriarch in 1853.
emer-harris.connections: He was an older brother of Martin Harris. His named companion is Simeon Carter (75:30).

sources.title: Emer Harris, Joseph Smith Papers biography

emma-smith.name: Emma Hale Smith
emma-smith.role: Wife of Joseph Smith, early scribe, and Relief Society president
emma-smith.dateNote: She was baptized at Colesville on 28 June 1830, and section 25 was given for her that July.
emma-smith.importance: Emma Hale married Joseph Smith in 1827 and wrote for him during the early Book of Mormon translation. Section 25 addresses her by name, calls her an “elect lady,” and asks her to select sacred hymns. She edited the Church’s 1835 hymnal and became president of the Nauvoo Female Relief Society in 1842. Section 132 of 1843 commands her to accept plural marriage, and she rejected that document.
emma-smith.connections: Daughter of Isaac and Elizabeth Hale of Harmony, Pennsylvania, and wife of Joseph Smith. After his death she married Lewis Bidamon in 1847 and joined the Reorganized Church in 1860.

sources.title: Emma Hale Smith, Joseph Smith Papers

enoch.name: Enoch
enoch.role: Ancient patriarch whose city was taken to God
enoch.dateNote: Section 107 says Adam ordained him at twenty-five and that he walked with God 365 years before being translated.
enoch.importance: Section 38 has the Lord speak as the one who took “the Zion of Enoch” into his own bosom. Section 45 says his people were received by God as “a city reserved until a day of righteousness.” Sections 84 and 107 place him in the priesthood line from Adam. Section 107 also mentions a book of Enoch to be testified of later.
enoch.connections: The D&C names Adam, who ordained him, and Methuselah and Noah among his posterity.

sources.title: Doctrine and Covenants 38
Doctrine and Covenants 107

erastus-snow.name: Erastus Snow
erastus-snow.dateNote: Section 136 assigned him to organize a company on 14 January 1847; he became an apostle on 12 February 1849.
erastus-snow.importance: Erastus Snow was baptized in Vermont in 1833, served many missions, and later lived at Montrose, Iowa. Section 136 tells him and Ezra T. Benson to organize a company for the trek west. He entered the Salt Lake Valley with the 1847 pioneer company. He became an apostle in 1849 and founded St. George, Utah, in 1861.
erastus-snow.connections: Section 136 pairs him with Ezra T. Benson.

sources.title: Erastus Snow, Joseph Smith Papers biography

eve.name: Eve
eve.role: First woman, called “Mother Eve” in section 138
eve.dateNote: Section 138 records Joseph F. Smith’s vision of 3 October 1918.
eve.importance: The vision in section 138 lists Eve among the righteous dead in the spirit world. It calls her “our glorious Mother Eve” and places her with “many of her faithful daughters” who worshiped the true God. She appears beside “Father Adam” in the same congregation.
eve.connections: Section 138 names her next to Adam.

sources.title: Doctrine and Covenants 138

ezra-booth.name: Ezra Booth
ezra-booth.role: Methodist minister who joined, then publicly opposed the Church
ezra-booth.dateNote: Section 52 sent him to Missouri in June 1831; he was barred from preaching on 6 September 1831.
ezra-booth.importance: Ezra Booth was a Methodist minister from Mantua, Ohio, who joined in 1831. Section 52 sends him to Missouri with Isaac Morley, but he was barred from preaching soon after his return. Section 64 says the Lord was angry with him and Morley for not keeping the law. From September 1831 he published nine letters against the Church, which prompted section 71.
ezra-booth.connections: His companion was Isaac Morley; Sidney Rigdon later challenged his published claims.

sources.title: Ezra Booth, Joseph Smith Papers biography

ezra-t-benson.name: Ezra T. Benson
ezra-t-benson.role: Apostle who led a pioneer company west
ezra-t-benson.dateNote: He was ordained an apostle on 16 July 1846 and named in section 136 on 14 January 1847.
ezra-t-benson.importance: Section 136 tells him and Erastus Snow to organize a company for the journey west. He went with Brigham Young’s first pioneer company, arriving in the Salt Lake Valley on 24 July 1847. He later sat in the Utah legislature and presided over the Cache Valley stake.
ezra-t-benson.connections: He worked with Brigham Young and Erastus Snow. He was baptized at Quincy, Illinois, in 1840.

sources.title: Ezra Taft Benson, Joseph Smith Papers

ezra-thayre.name: Ezra Thayre
ezra-thayre.role: Early convert and missionary from New York
ezra-thayre.dateNote: He was baptized in fall 1830; section 33 dates from October 1830 and section 56 from June 1831.
ezra-thayre.importance: Section 33 calls him and Northrop Sweet to preach soon after their baptism. Section 52 sends him to Missouri with Thomas B. Marsh. Section 56 cancels that mission because he was not ready and tells him to repent of pride and selfishness. Section 75 pairs him with Marsh again in January 1832.
ezra-thayre.connections: Parley P. Pratt baptized him. His named companions are Northrop Sweet and Thomas B. Marsh.

sources.title: Ezra Thayre, Joseph Smith Papers biography

frederick-g-williams.name: Frederick G. Williams
frederick-g-williams.role: Scribe and counselor in the First Presidency
frederick-g-williams.dateNote: He became Joseph Smith’s scribe in July 1832 and was ordained a counselor in the presidency on 18 March 1833.
frederick-g-williams.importance: A Kirtland physician baptized in 1830, he was told in section 64 not to sell his farm. He wrote down several revelations, including sections 84 and 87. Section 81, first given to Jesse Gause, later carried his name, and section 90 counts him equal with the presidency. Later revelations direct work on the temple, a home for his family, and the printing office he ran with Oliver Cowdery.
frederick-g-williams.connections: Husband of Rebecca Swain Williams. He served with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon in the presidency and with Hyrum Smith and others on temple and printing work.

sources.title: Frederick Granger Williams, Joseph Smith Papers

george-a-smith.name: George A. Smith
george-a-smith.role: Apostle, cousin of Joseph Smith, and Church historian
george-a-smith.dateNote: He was ordained an apostle at Far West on 26 April 1839 and named in section 136 in January 1847.
george-a-smith.importance: He marched with Zion’s Camp in 1834 and became a Seventy in 1835. Section 124 lists him among the Twelve. Section 136 tells him and Amasa Lyman to organize a company for the trek west. In Utah he became Church historian and later first counselor to Brigham Young.
george-a-smith.connections: Son of John Smith and Clarissa Lyman, which made him Joseph Smith’s first cousin. He served with Amasa Lyman and the other apostles.

sources.title: George A. Smith, Joseph Smith Papers

george-miller.name: George Miller
george-miller.role: Nauvoo bishop and Nauvoo House trustee
george-miller.dateNote: He was baptized in August 1839 and appointed a bishop by section 124 on 19 January 1841.
george-miller.importance: Section 124 calls him “without guile” and gives him the office of a bishopric like Edward Partridge’s. It also names him first among the men to build the Nauvoo House, a boarding house for visitors. He led the 1842–1843 expedition to the Wisconsin pineries for temple and Nauvoo House lumber. He later broke with Brigham Young and was excommunicated in 1848.
george-miller.connections: He worked with Lyman Wight, John Snider, and Peter Haws on the Nauvoo House. He later associated with Lyman Wight’s group and then James Strang’s followers.

sources.title: George Miller, Joseph Smith Papers

gideon-carter.name: Gideon Carter
gideon-carter.role: Early elder killed at Crooked River
gideon-carter.dateNote: He was baptized on 25 October 1831 and killed at Crooked River, Missouri, on 25 October 1838.
gideon-carter.importance: He was ordained an elder at the Amherst conference, and section 75 pairs him there with Sylvester Smith for a mission. He later served on the Kirtland high council. He moved to Far West in 1838 and was killed at the Crooked River skirmish.
gideon-carter.connections: His companion in section 75 was Sylvester Smith. David W. Patten was also mortally wounded at Crooked River.

sources.title: Gideon Hayden Carter, Joseph Smith Papers biography

harvey-whitlock.name: Harvey Whitlock
harvey-whitlock.role: Early elder sent to Missouri in 1831
harvey-whitlock.dateNote: He was ordained a high priest on 4 June 1831; section 52 sends him to Missouri two days later.
harvey-whitlock.importance: Section 52 sends him with David Whitmer to preach on the way to Missouri. Joseph Smith’s party met him at Chariton in August 1831 (62). He settled in Missouri and was driven from Jackson County in 1833. He was excommunicated by 1835, and his later life moved between several churches.
harvey-whitlock.connections: His companion in section 52 was David Whitmer. He met Hyrum Smith and John Murdock at Chariton.

sources.title: Harvey Gilman Whitlock, Joseph Smith Papers biography

heber-c-kimball.name: Heber C. Kimball
heber-c-kimball.role: Member of the first Quorum of the Twelve
heber-c-kimball.dateNote: He was ordained an apostle on 14 February 1835 and led the first mission to Britain in 1837.
heber-c-kimball.importance: Heber C. Kimball was a potter from Mendon, New York, baptized in April 1832. He became one of the first Twelve Apostles in 1835. In June 1837 he left Kirtland to open the mission in England, the background to section 112. Section 124 lists him among the Twelve at Nauvoo, and he later served as first counselor to Brigham Young.
heber-c-kimball.connections: He married Vilate Murray in 1822. He served beside Brigham Young, Orson Hyde, and the other apostles named in section 124.

sources.title: Heber Chase Kimball, Joseph Smith Papers biography

henry-g-sherwood.name: Henry G. Sherwood
henry-g-sherwood.role: High councilor, Nauvoo marshal, and Nauvoo House stockholder
henry-g-sherwood.dateNote: Section 124 named him in January 1841 as a Nauvoo House stockholder and high councilor.
henry-g-sherwood.importance: Section 124 invites him to pay stock into the Nauvoo House for himself and his descendants. It also confirms him on the Nauvoo high council, where he had served since 1839. He was Nauvoo city marshal from 1841 to 1843. He crossed to the Salt Lake Valley in 1847 but later became disaffected and died in San Bernardino.
henry-g-sherwood.connections: He was ordained an elder by Jared and Simeon Carter. He served on the high council with Newel Knight, Samuel Bent, and others named in section 124.

sources.title: Henry Garlick Sherwood, Joseph Smith Papers

hiram-page.name: Hiram Page
hiram-page.role: Book of Mormon witness who claimed revelations through a stone
hiram-page.dateNote: He was one of the Eight Witnesses in June 1829 and was baptized on 11 April 1830; section 28 dates from September 1830.
hiram-page.importance: In 1830 he said he received revelations for the Church through a stone, and some members accepted them. Section 28 tells Oliver Cowdery to tell him privately that those writings were not from the Lord. He later renounced the writings after that revelation. He later moved with the Saints to Ohio and Missouri and left the Church in 1838.
hiram-page.connections: He married Catherine Whitmer in 1825, so the Whitmer brothers were his brothers-in-law. Section 28 sends Oliver Cowdery to speak with him.

sources.title: Hiram Page, Joseph Smith Papers biography

hyrum-smith.name: Hyrum Smith
hyrum-smith.role: Joseph Smith’s older brother, Church patriarch and Assistant President
hyrum-smith.dateNote: He was baptized in June 1829, named patriarch in the January 1841 revelation, and killed with Joseph at Carthage on 27 June 1844.
hyrum-smith.importance: Section 11 answers his wish to help in May 1829 by telling him to prepare before he preaches. In Kirtland he was named to the committee to build the Lord’s house (sections 94–95). He shared Liberty Jail with Joseph in 1838–1839. Section 124 praises his integrity and makes him patriarch, and section 135 reports his death beside Joseph.
hyrum-smith.connections: He was the son of Joseph Smith Sr. and Lucy Mack Smith and an older brother of Joseph and Samuel H. Smith. He worked with Reynolds Cahoon and Jared Carter on the Kirtland building committee and was the father of Joseph F. Smith.

sources.title: Hyrum Smith, Joseph Smith Papers biography

isaac-galland.name: Isaac Galland
isaac-galland.role: Land seller at Commerce and in Iowa
isaac-galland.dateNote: He sold land to the Saints in 1839 and was baptized on 3 July 1839; section 124 is dated 19 January 1841.
isaac-galland.importance: Isaac Galland was a doctor and land speculator on both sides of the Mississippi. In 1839 he sold the Saints land at Commerce and about 19,000 acres in Iowa’s Half-Breed Tract, and Joseph Smith baptized him that July. Section 124 says the Lord loves him for his work, tells him to buy Nauvoo House stock, and sends him with Hyrum Smith. He acted as a Church land agent but withdrew about 1842.
isaac-galland.connections: Section 124 names William Marks to ordain him and Hyrum Smith as his companion.

sources.title: Isaac Galland, Joseph Smith Papers biography

isaac-morley.name: Isaac Morley
isaac-morley.role: Kirtland farmer, bishop’s counselor, and later patriarch
isaac-morley.dateNote: He was baptized on 15 November 1830, and the Morley farm was ordered sold in September 1831.
isaac-morley.importance: Early converts and the New York Saints gathered on his Kirtland farm. Section 52 sends him with Ezra Booth to Missouri in June 1831. Section 64 says he and Booth had kept neither law nor commandment, but that Morley was forgiven. It explains that his farm was sold so he would not be tempted beyond what he could bear.
isaac-morley.connections: He was a counselor to Bishop Edward Partridge in Ohio and Missouri. Titus Billings married his younger sister Diantha and cared for the farm.

sources.title: Isaac Morley, Joseph Smith Papers
Titus Billings, Wikipedia

james-covel.name: James Covel
james-covel.role: Methodist minister who covenanted to obey, then left
james-covel.dateNote: Sections 39 and 40 were given on 5 and 6 January 1831 at Fayette.
james-covel.importance: Section 39 tells a minister named James that he should be baptized and preach. Section 40, given a day later, says his heart had been right but fear and worldly cares led him to reject the word. Joseph Smith’s history says he returned to his former principles and people.
james-covel.connections: He dealt with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon at Fayette. He had been a Methodist preacher for decades and helped ordain the first elders of the AME Zion Church in 1822.

sources.title: James Covel, Joseph Smith Papers

jared-carter.name: Jared Carter
jared-carter.role: Missionary and Kirtland temple committee member
jared-carter.dateNote: Section 79 sent him east on 12 March 1832, and section 94 named him to the building committee in August 1833.
jared-carter.importance: Jared Carter was baptized at Colesville in February 1831 and moved with that branch to Ohio. Section 79 sends him again to preach in the eastern states. Section 94 names him to the Kirtland building committee with Hyrum Smith and Reynolds Cahoon, and section 102 lists him on the high council. In Missouri in 1838 he was briefly a leader among the Danites; he later moved to Nauvoo.
jared-carter.connections: His brothers John S. Carter and Simeon D. Carter also served as elders. He worked with Hyrum Smith and Reynolds Cahoon on the temple.

sources.title: Jared Carter, Joseph Smith Papers biography

jesse-gause.name: Jesse Gause
jesse-gause.dateNote: Joseph Smith chose him as counselor on 8 March 1832, and section 81 was first addressed to him on 15 March.
jesse-gause.importance: Jesse Gause was a former Quaker and Shaker whom Joseph Smith chose as a counselor on 8 March 1832. The revelation now in section 81 was first written to him, then readdressed to Frederick G. Williams. He went with Joseph to Missouri in spring 1832 and is listed in the United Firm. He left a mission in August 1832 and was apparently excommunicated that December.
jesse-gause.connections: He served with Sidney Rigdon and travelled with Zebedee Coltrin on his 1832 mission.

sources.title: Jesse Gause, Joseph Smith Papers biography

jesus-christ.name: Jesus Christ
jesus-christ.role: The Lord who speaks in most D&C revelations
jesus-christ.dateNote: Section 76 reports a vision of him on 16 February 1832, and section 110 one on 3 April 1836.
jesus-christ.importance: Most D&C revelations present their speaker as Jesus Christ, and section 45 has him plead as an advocate with the Father. Section 76 reports that Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon saw him at the right hand of God. Section 110 reports that he appeared in the Kirtland temple and accepted the house. Section 138 describes his visit to the spirits of the dead.
jesus-christ.connections: He addresses Joseph Smith and many early members by name. The revelations present him as sending John the Baptist, Peter, James, John, Moses, Elias, and Elijah.

sources.title: Doctrine and Covenants 110

john-c-bennett.name: John C. Bennett
john-c-bennett.role: Nauvoo mayor and assistant president who turned critic
john-c-bennett.dateNote: He was baptized in September 1840, praised in section 124 in January 1841, and excommunicated on 11 May 1842.
john-c-bennett.importance: A physician and militia officer, Bennett helped secure the Nauvoo charter in 1840. Section 124 tells him to help Joseph Smith send the word abroad and promises reward “if he receive counsel.” He became mayor of Nauvoo and assistant president, then was excommunicated for adultery in 1842. He then accused Joseph Smith of adultery and of plotting the attack on Lilburn Boggs, which led to the hiding behind section 127.
john-c-bennett.connections: He worked with Joseph Smith and the Nauvoo city government. After leaving he aided Missouri and Illinois officials seeking Joseph’s arrest, and later joined James Strang’s movement for a time.

sources.title: John Cook Bennett, Joseph Smith Papers

john-corrill.name: John Corrill
john-corrill.role: Missouri bishop’s counselor and early Church historian
john-corrill.dateNote: He was baptized on 10 January 1831 and named in sections 50 and 52 in May and June 1831.
john-corrill.importance: John Corrill was baptized at Kirtland in January 1831. Section 50 names him among elders sent to strengthen the churches, and section 52 sends him to Missouri with Lyman Wight. He served as counselor to Bishop Edward Partridge, and in 1838 was a Missouri legislator and Church historian. He testified against Joseph Smith that November, was excommunicated in March 1839, and published a history of the Church.
john-corrill.connections: He worked with Edward Partridge and Lyman Wight in Missouri.

sources.title: John Corrill, Joseph Smith Papers biography

john-e-page.name: John E. Page
john-e-page.role: Member of the Quorum of the Twelve, 1838–1846
john-e-page.dateNote: Section 118 named him to the Twelve on 8 July 1838; he was ordained on 19 December 1838.
john-e-page.importance: John E. Page was baptized in Ohio in 1833 and in 1838 led a company of converts from Upper Canada to Missouri. Section 118 names him to fill one of the vacancies in the Twelve. Section 124 lists him among the apostles in 1841. He was removed from the Twelve and excommunicated in 1846, and later backed James Strang and other groups.
john-e-page.connections: Section 118 names him with John Taylor, Wilford Woodruff, and Willard Richards. Emer Harris baptized him.

sources.title: John Edward Page, Joseph Smith Papers biography

john-gould.name: John Gould
john-gould.role: Messenger to Missouri in 1833 and later Seventy president
john-gould.dateNote: He was baptized on 16 December 1832 and went to Missouri with Orson Hyde in August 1833.
john-gould.importance: In August 1833 he and Orson Hyde carried Joseph Smith’s instructions to the Church leaders in Missouri. Section 100 assures Joseph that the two are “in my hands.” They returned with news of the Jackson County violence, which stands behind section 101. He later recruited for the Camp of Israel and served as a president of the Seventy in 1837.
john-gould.connections: Reynolds Cahoon baptized him, and his companion to Missouri was Orson Hyde.

sources.title: John Gould, Joseph Smith Papers biography

john-johnson.name: John Johnson
john-johnson.role: Hiram farmer who hosted Joseph Smith
john-johnson.dateNote: Joseph Smith lived in his Hiram home in 1831–1832; he joined the United Firm on 4 June 1833.
john-johnson.importance: Joseph Smith lived and received many revelations in his home at Hiram, Ohio. Section 96 accepts his offering and admits him to the United Firm in June 1833. Section 102 names him to the first Kirtland high council, and section 104 assigns him property. He became disaffected from the Church in 1837–1838.
john-johnson.connections: He married Alice (Elsa) Jacobs in 1800. He was the father of Lyman and Luke Johnson.

sources.title: John Johnson, Joseph Smith Papers biography

john-murdock.name: John Murdock
john-murdock.dateNote: He was baptized on 5 November 1830; section 99 calls him on a mission in August 1832.
john-murdock.importance: Section 52 sends him to Missouri with Hyrum Smith by way of Detroit in June 1831. He fell ill on the way and stayed at Chariton, where Joseph Smith met him (62). Section 99 calls him to preach in the eastern countries after providing for his children.
john-murdock.connections: His wife Julia Clapp died in 1831 after giving birth to twins, whom Joseph and Emma Smith adopted. Hyrum Smith was his companion in sections 52 and 62.

sources.title: John Murdock, Joseph Smith Papers biography

john-s-carter.name: John S. Carter
john-s-carter.role: Member of the first Kirtland high council
john-s-carter.dateNote: Section 102 lists him on the high council organized in February 1834; he died that June in Missouri.
john-s-carter.importance: John S. Carter joined about 1832 in Vermont and preached there with his brother Jared. Section 102 lists him among the twelve councilors of the first Kirtland high council in 1834. He then marched with the camp to Missouri. He died in Clay County, Missouri, in late June 1834.
john-s-carter.connections: He was a brother of Jared Carter and Simeon D. Carter.

sources.title: John Sims Carter, Joseph Smith Papers biography

john-smith.name: John Smith (1781–1854)
john-smith.role: Uncle of Joseph Smith, high councilor, and later patriarch
john-smith.dateNote: He was named to the first Kirtland high council in February 1834.
john-smith.importance: Section 102 lists him among the twelve high priests chosen as the first standing high council at Kirtland. From 1837 to 1844 he was an assistant counselor in the First Presidency. He later presided over the stake in Lee County, Iowa, and the first Salt Lake Stake. He became Presiding Patriarch in 1849.
john-smith.connections: Brother of Joseph Smith Sr. and uncle of Joseph and Hyrum Smith. Father of the apostle George A. Smith.

sources.title: John Smith (uncle of Joseph Smith), Wikipedia
George A. Smith, Joseph Smith Papers

john-snider.name: John Snider
john-snider.dateNote: He was baptized in Toronto in 1836; section 124 names him in January 1841.
john-snider.importance: Section 124 names him with George Miller, Lyman Wight, and Peter Haws to build the Nauvoo House. It tells them to use stock only for that house. He also served missions to Britain in 1837 and 1842–1843.
john-snider.connections: He worked with George Miller, Lyman Wight, and Peter Haws on the Nauvoo House. He married Mary Heron in 1822.

sources.title: John Snider (Snyder), Joseph Smith Papers biography

john-taylor.name: John Taylor
john-taylor.role: Apostle wounded at Carthage, later Church president
john-taylor.dateNote: He was called to the Twelve in July 1838 and ordained that December; he was wounded at Carthage on 27 June 1844.
john-taylor.importance: Section 118 names him to fill a vacancy in the Twelve in July 1838. Section 124 lists him with the Twelve at Nauvoo. He was in the Carthage Jail room when Joseph and Hyrum Smith were killed, and section 135 reports he was badly wounded. Section 138 names him among the leaders seen in Joseph F. Smith’s vision.
john-taylor.connections: Parley P. Pratt baptized him in Canada in 1836. Willard Richards was with him at Carthage, and he later succeeded Brigham Young as Church president.

sources.title: John Taylor, Joseph Smith Papers biography

john-the-baptist.name: John the Baptist
john-the-baptist.role: New Testament prophet who restored the Aaronic Priesthood
john-the-baptist.dateNote: The D&C reports his visit near Harmony, Pennsylvania, on 15 May 1829.
john-the-baptist.importance: Section 13 gives the words of an angel who, Joseph Smith reported, conferred the Priesthood of Aaron on him and Oliver Cowdery. The revelation in section 27 says this John, son of Zacharias, was sent to ordain them. Section 35 compares Sidney Rigdon to John, sent to prepare the way. Section 84 says he was ordained by an angel at eight days old to prepare for the Lord’s coming.
john-the-baptist.connections: The D&C names his father Zacharias and links him with Elias. The section 13 heading says he acted under Peter, James, and John.

sources.title: Doctrine and Covenants 13
Doctrine and Covenants 27
Doctrine and Covenants 84

john-the-revelator.name: John the Revelator
john-the-revelator.role: Apostle of Jesus and writer of the book of Revelation
john-the-revelator.dateNote: Section 77, about March 1832, answers questions on his book of Revelation.
john-the-revelator.importance: Section 77 answers questions about the symbols John saw, such as the sea of glass, the four beasts, and the sealed book. It says the little book he ate was a mission to gather the tribes of Israel, as an Elias who restores all things. Section 7 says he asked to remain on earth to bring souls to Christ. Section 128 cites his vision of the dead being judged from the books.
john-the-revelator.connections: The D&C names him with Peter and James as the apostles who conferred keys in section 27.

sources.title: Doctrine and Covenants 77
Doctrine and Covenants 27

john-whitmer.name: John Whitmer
john-whitmer.role: Scribe and first appointed Church historian
john-whitmer.dateNote: He was baptized in June 1829, appointed Church historian in March 1831, and excommunicated at Far West in March 1838.
john-whitmer.importance: Section 15 answers his wish to know what would be most worth to him in June 1829. He served as a scribe and copied revelations for Joseph Smith. Section 47 names him to keep a regular history, and section 69 sends him to Missouri with the revelations and Oliver Cowdery. Section 70 makes him a steward over the revelations.
john-whitmer.connections: He was a son of Peter Whitmer Sr. and a brother of David and Peter Whitmer Jr. Section 30 sends him to preach near the home of Philip Burroughs.

sources.title: John Whitmer, Joseph Smith Papers biography

joseph-coe.name: Joseph Coe
joseph-coe.role: Early elder and Kirtland high councilor
joseph-coe.dateNote: Section 55 sent him to Missouri in June 1831, and section 102 lists him on the first high council in February 1834.
joseph-coe.importance: Joseph Coe, a New York farmer, joined in 1831; section 55 sends him to Missouri with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon. Section 102 names him to the first Kirtland high council in 1834. In 1835 he paid a third of the price of the Egyptian mummies and papyri. He was excommunicated in December 1837.
joseph-coe.connections: He travelled with Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon, and William W. Phelps in 1831.

sources.title: Joseph Coe, Joseph Smith Papers biography

joseph-f-smith.name: Joseph F. Smith
joseph-f-smith.role: Sixth President of the Church; received section 138
joseph-f-smith.dateNote: He reported the vision in section 138 on 3 October 1918, about six weeks before his death on 19 November 1918.
joseph-f-smith.importance: Section 138 is his account of a vision of the spirit world, received while he pondered Christ’s visit to the dead. The vision says the Savior organized faithful spirits to preach to those in prison. It names many he saw there, including his father Hyrum Smith. The text was later added to the scriptures.
joseph-f-smith.connections: He was the son of Hyrum Smith and Mary Fielding Smith and a nephew of Joseph Smith. He served as Church president from 1901 to 1918.

sources.title: Joseph F. Smith, Church History Topics
Joseph F. Smith, Wikipedia

joseph-knight-sr.name: Joseph Knight Sr.
joseph-knight-sr.role: Early supporter of Joseph Smith from Colesville, New York
joseph-knight-sr.dateNote: Section 12 came in May 1829, when he brought supplies to Harmony; he was baptized on 28 June 1830.
joseph-knight-sr.importance: Joseph Knight Sr. was a farmer and miller who had hired Joseph Smith in 1826. In May 1829 he brought paper and food to Harmony so translation could go on, and section 12 answered his question about his duty. Section 23 tells him to pray vocally and join the Church. His family formed the core of the Colesville branch, which moved to Thompson, Ohio, and then to Jackson County, Missouri, in 1831.
joseph-knight-sr.connections: His wife Polly died in Missouri on 7 August 1831, the day section 59 was given; his son Newel Knight led the Colesville branch.

sources.title: Joseph Knight Sr., Joseph Smith Papers biography
Joseph Knight Sr., Wikipedia

joseph-smith-sr.name: Joseph Smith Sr.
joseph-smith-sr.role: Father of Joseph Smith and first patriarch of the Church
joseph-smith-sr.dateNote: He was baptized on 6 April 1830, the day the Church was organized, and ordained patriarch on 6 December 1834.
joseph-smith-sr.importance: Section 4 was given for him in February 1829, when he visited his son at Harmony. He was one of the Eight Witnesses, and section 23 calls him to exhort and strengthen the Church. In Kirtland he sat on the first high council in 1834 and became the Church’s patriarch. Section 90 lets him keep his home, and section 124 says after his death that he “sitteth with Abraham.”
joseph-smith-sr.connections: Husband of Lucy Mack Smith and father of Alvin, Hyrum, Joseph, Samuel, William, Don Carlos, and others. In section 137 Joseph reports seeing his father and mother in the celestial kingdom, while both were still living.

sources.title: Joseph Smith Sr., Joseph Smith Papers

joseph-smith.name: Joseph Smith Jr.
joseph-smith.role: Prophet and founding leader of the Church
joseph-smith.dateNote: He reported the angel’s visit of September 1823, organized the Church on 6 April 1830, and was killed at Carthage on 27 June 1844.
joseph-smith.importance: Nearly every revelation in the Doctrine and Covenants came through him, from Harmony and Fayette to Kirtland, Missouri, and Nauvoo. He dictated revelations, organized the Church in 1830, and led its moves west. He wrote sections 121–123 as letters from Liberty Jail. Section 135 reports his death with his brother Hyrum at Carthage Jail.
joseph-smith.connections: He was the son of Joseph Smith Sr. and Lucy Mack Smith and married Emma Hale in 1827. Hyrum Smith, Oliver Cowdery, and Sidney Rigdon worked most closely with him in these sections.

sources.title: Joseph Smith Jr., Church History Topics
Joseph Smith, Wikipedia

joseph-wakefield.name: Joseph Wakefield
joseph-wakefield.role: Early elder who later turned against the Church
joseph-wakefield.dateNote: He was named in revelations of May and June 1831 and was excommunicated by January 1834.
joseph-wakefield.importance: Section 50 sends him with Parley P. Pratt and John Corrill to strengthen the churches in May 1831. Section 52 sends him to the eastern lands with Solomon Humphrey. On a later mission in New York he baptized George A. Smith. He was excommunicated by 1834 and joined actions against the Saints in Kirtland.
joseph-wakefield.connections: His companions in these sections were Parley P. Pratt and Solomon Humphrey.

sources.title: Joseph H. Wakefield, Joseph Smith Papers biography
Joseph H. Wakefield, Doctrine and Covenants Central

leman-copley.name: Leman Copley
leman-copley.role: Former Shaker convert who owned land at Thompson, Ohio
leman-copley.dateNote: Section 49 sent him to the Shakers in May 1831, and by June he had broken his land agreement.
leman-copley.importance: Leman Copley was a former Shaker who joined the Church by 1831. He offered land at Thompson, Ohio, where the Colesville Saints settled. Section 49 sends him with Sidney Rigdon and Parley P. Pratt to preach to the Shakers, teaching only what they teach him. After that mission he went back on the agreement and ordered the Colesville members off his land, the event behind section 54.
leman-copley.connections: He deals with Sidney Rigdon, Parley P. Pratt, and the Colesville branch led by Newel Knight.

sources.title: Leman Copley, Joseph Smith Papers biography

levi-w-hancock.name: Levi W. Hancock
levi-w-hancock.role: Early missionary and a president of the Seventy
levi-w-hancock.dateNote: He was baptized on 16 November 1830 and called to Missouri by section 52 in June 1831.
levi-w-hancock.importance: Section 52 sends him with Zebedee Coltrin to Missouri, preaching on the way. His later autobiography is a key account of the June 1831 conference behind that section. He marched with Zion’s Camp in 1834 and became one of the presidents of the Seventy in 1835. Section 124 confirms him in that role as “Levi Hancock.”
levi-w-hancock.connections: He traveled with Zebedee Coltrin and later served with Joseph Young among the Seventy’s presidents. He was the only general authority in the Mormon Battalion.

sources.title: Levi Ward Hancock, Joseph Smith Papers

lucy-mack-smith.name: Lucy Mack Smith
lucy-mack-smith.dateNote: Joseph Smith’s vision of 21 January 1836 places her in the celestial kingdom while she was still living.
lucy-mack-smith.importance: Lucy Mack Smith is not named in the D&C, but section 137 says Joseph saw “my father and my mother” in the celestial kingdom. She was baptized on 6 April 1830, the day the Church was organized. In May 1831 she led a company of Fayette branch members to Kirtland. She later wrote a history of the Smith family, published in 1853.
lucy-mack-smith.connections: She married Joseph Smith Sr. in 1796; their children included Alvin, Hyrum, Joseph, and Samuel H. Smith. Section 137 places her beside her husband and her son Alvin.

sources.title: Lucy Mack Smith, Joseph Smith Papers biography

luke-johnson.name: Luke S. Johnson
luke-johnson.role: Missionary and member of the first Quorum of the Twelve
luke-johnson.dateNote: Section 68 was given to him and others on 1 November 1831; he became an apostle in February 1835.
luke-johnson.importance: Luke Johnson, a son of John Johnson of Hiram, was baptized in May 1831 and sent to preach in section 68. Section 75 pairs him with William E. McLellin, and section 102 lists him on the high council. He was one of the first Twelve Apostles from 1835 until he broke with Joseph Smith in late 1837. He was excommunicated in 1838, rebaptized in 1846, and went west in 1847.
luke-johnson.connections: His father John Johnson and brother Lyman E. Johnson also appear in the D&C. Orson Hyde, his brother-in-law, rebaptized him.

sources.title: Luke Johnson, Joseph Smith Papers biography
Luke Johnson, Wikipedia

lyman-johnson.name: Lyman E. Johnson
lyman-johnson.role: Early missionary and member of the first Twelve
lyman-johnson.dateNote: He was baptized in February 1831, became an apostle in 1835, and was excommunicated on 13 April 1838.
lyman-johnson.importance: Section 68 answers his request, with three other elders, to know the Lord’s will in November 1831. Section 75 sends him east with Orson Pratt. He was one of the original Twelve Apostles in 1835. He was excommunicated in April 1838, and section 118 fills the vacancies left in the Twelve.
lyman-johnson.connections: He was a son of John and Elsa Johnson of Hiram, Ohio, and a brother of Luke Johnson. His companions in these sections were Orson Pratt, Orson Hyde, and William E. McLellin.

sources.title: Lyman Eugene Johnson, Joseph Smith Papers biography

lyman-sherman.name: Lyman R. Sherman
lyman-sherman.role: One of the first presidents of the Seventy
lyman-sherman.dateNote: He became a president of the Seventy on 28 February 1835; section 108 dates from 26 December 1835.
lyman-sherman.importance: Section 108 answers his request to know his duty and says his sins are forgiven. It tells him to wait to be remembered with the first elders. He was called to the Twelve in January 1839 but died at Far West before he was told or ordained.
lyman-sherman.connections: He married Delcena Didamia Johnson in 1829. He served with the other presidents of the Seventy called in 1835.

sources.title: Lyman Royal Sherman, Joseph Smith Papers biography

lyman-wight.name: Lyman Wight
lyman-wight.role: Missouri leader and later member of the Twelve
lyman-wight.dateNote: Section 52 named him in June 1831, and he was ordained an apostle on 8 April 1841.
lyman-wight.importance: Lyman Wight joined in November 1830, and section 52 sends him to Missouri with a warning that Satan desires to sift him. Section 103 sends him to raise volunteers for Zion in 1834. He lived at Adam-ondi-Ahman and was jailed with Joseph Smith in Missouri in 1838–39. Section 124 calls him to preach and help build the Nauvoo House; he later led a group to Texas and was excommunicated in 1848.
lyman-wight.connections: He travels with John Corrill, Parley P. Pratt, and Sidney Rigdon. In section 124 he works with George Miller, John Snider, and Peter Haws.

sources.title: Lyman Wight, Joseph Smith Papers biography

major-n-ashley.name: Major N. Ashley
major-n-ashley.role: Early elder sent south on a mission in 1832
major-n-ashley.dateNote: Section 75, dated 25 January 1832, sends him on a mission.
major-n-ashley.importance: Major Noble Ashley lived in Strongsville, Ohio, and joined the Church by June 1831. He was ordained an elder in October 1831. Section 75 sends him with Burr Riggs into “the south country.” He had left the Church by 1838.
major-n-ashley.connections: His named companion is Burr Riggs (75:17).

sources.title: Major Noble Ashley, Joseph Smith Papers biography

martin-harris.name: Martin Harris
martin-harris.role: Book of Mormon scribe, printing financier, and witness
martin-harris.dateNote: He lost the 116 manuscript pages in June 1828 and became one of the Three Witnesses in June 1829.
martin-harris.importance: A Palmyra farmer, Harris wrote for Joseph Smith in 1828 and then lost the first 116 pages, the loss behind sections 3 and 10. Section 5 promises him a witness, and section 17 names him with the Three Witnesses. Section 19 urges him to pay for printing, and he later sold land to cover the cost. Later revelations send him to Missouri, make him an example of consecration, and place him on the Kirtland high council.
martin-harris.connections: Husband of Lucy Harris, who opposed the Book of Mormon. He worked with Joseph Smith, Oliver Cowdery, David Whitmer, and the members of the United Firm.

sources.title: Martin Harris, Joseph Smith Papers

micah-b-welton.name: Micah B. Welton
micah-b-welton.role: Early Ohio convert sent on a mission in 1832
micah-b-welton.dateNote: He was baptized on 23 June 1831, and section 75 named him on 25 January 1832.
micah-b-welton.importance: Micah B. Welton lived in Medina County, Ohio, and was baptized in June 1831. Section 75 pairs him with Eden Smith for a mission. He later lived in Clay County, Missouri, and then in Illinois. He was ordained a Seventy in 1839.
micah-b-welton.connections: His named companion is Eden Smith (75:36).

sources.title: Micah Baldwin Welton, Joseph Smith Papers biography

moroni.name: Moroni
moroni.role: Angel who revealed the Book of Mormon record
moroni.dateNote: The official heading to section 2 dates his visit to Joseph Smith to the evening of 21 September 1823.
moroni.importance: The heading to section 2 identifies the messenger who spoke to Joseph Smith in 1823 as Moroni. Section 27 says Moroni was sent to reveal the Book of Mormon and holds “the keys of the record of the stick of Ephraim.” In section 128 Joseph Smith recalls the voice of Moroni “from Cumorah.” Section 138 says Moroni spoke to Joseph Smith of Elijah’s coming.
moroni.connections: The revelations present him as the last keeper of the Book of Mormon record. Section 27 lists him with Elias, Elijah, and Peter, James, and John.

sources.title: Doctrine and Covenants 2 (official text and heading)
Doctrine and Covenants 27 (official text)

moses.name: Moses
moses.role: Ancient prophet and lawgiver of Israel
moses.dateNote: Section 110 reports his appearance in the Kirtland temple on 3 April 1836.
moses.importance: The D&C refers to Moses many times as a model prophet; section 28 says Joseph Smith receives revelation “even as Moses.” Section 8 links Oliver Cowdery’s gift to the spirit by which Moses led Israel through the Red Sea. Section 84 says Israel would not endure God’s presence, so Moses and the higher priesthood were taken. Section 110 says Moses appeared in the Kirtland temple and committed the keys of the gathering of Israel.
moses.connections: He is named with Jethro and Aaron in section 84, and with Elias and Elijah in section 110. Section 138 lists him among the righteous spirits.

sources.title: Doctrine and Covenants 110
Doctrine and Covenants 84
Doctrine and Covenants 138

nathanael.name: Nathanael
nathanael.role: Disciple of Jesus, named as a model of guilelessness
nathanael.dateNote: Section 41, dated 4 February 1831, compares Edward Partridge to him.
nathanael.importance: Nathanael is a disciple of Jesus in the Gospel of John. Section 41 calls Edward Partridge to be bishop. The revelation says this is because Partridge’s heart is pure, “like unto Nathanael of old, in whom there is no guile.”
nathanael.connections: He is named only as a comparison for Edward Partridge.

sources.title: Doctrine and Covenants 41

newel-k-whitney.name: Newel K. Whitney
newel-k-whitney.dateNote: He was baptized in November 1830 and called as bishop in Ohio in December 1831; section 117 tells him to leave Kirtland in July 1838.
newel-k-whitney.importance: Section 72 names him bishop in Ohio, alongside Edward Partridge in Missouri. His Kirtland store held the translating room and hosted the school of the prophets. Section 84 sends him to warn New York, Albany, and Boston, and section 93 tells him to set his family in order. Section 117 rebukes his “littleness of soul” and tells him to leave Kirtland.
newel-k-whitney.connections: He married Elizabeth Ann Smith and had been the business partner of Sidney Gilbert. He served with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon in the United Firm (78, 82, 104).

sources.title: Newel Kimball Whitney, Joseph Smith Papers biography

newel-knight.name: Newel Knight
newel-knight.dateNote: He was baptized in late May 1830 and led the Colesville Saints to Ohio and Missouri in 1831.
newel-knight.importance: Joseph Smith’s history reports that he cast an evil spirit out of Newel Knight in 1830, before his baptism. Section 52 calls him to be ordained and to travel with Selah J. Griffin. Section 54 answers his question when the Colesville Saints lost their place at Thompson, telling them to flee to Missouri. Section 56 then lets him stay with them and lead them west, and section 124 names him to the Nauvoo high council.
newel-knight.connections: Son of Joseph Knight Sr. and a leader of the Colesville families. He married Lydia Goldthwaite Bailey in 1835, and he died at Ponca on the trek west.

sources.title: Newel Knight, Joseph Smith Papers
Newel Knight, Wikipedia

northrop-sweet.name: Northrop Sweet
northrop-sweet.role: Early convert called to preach who soon left
northrop-sweet.dateNote: He was baptized by October 1830, and section 33 was given for him and Ezra Thayre that month.
northrop-sweet.importance: Section 33 calls him and Ezra Thayre to open their mouths and preach repentance. It tells them the field is white for harvest and to build the Church on the Lord’s rock. He moved to Kirtland and was ordained an elder by June 1831. Soon after, he left and helped found a small group called the Pure Church of Christ.
northrop-sweet.connections: Baptized by Parley P. Pratt and called with Ezra Thayre. He later farmed in Branch County, Michigan.

sources.title: Northrop Sweet, Joseph Smith Papers

oliver-cowdery.name: Oliver Cowdery
oliver-cowdery.role: Book of Mormon scribe and Second Elder of the Church
oliver-cowdery.dateNote: He began writing for Joseph Smith in April 1829 and is named second elder when the Church was organized on 6 April 1830.
oliver-cowdery.importance: Oliver Cowdery was Joseph Smith’s main scribe for the Book of Mormon at Harmony in 1829. Early revelations speak to his wish to translate, and sections 13 and 27 say he and Joseph received priesthood from heavenly messengers. He was one of the Three Witnesses, led the 1830–31 mission to the Lamanites, and helped print the revelations in Missouri. Section 110 reports that he shared Joseph’s visions in the Kirtland temple in 1836; he was excommunicated in 1838 and readmitted in 1848.
oliver-cowdery.connections: He married Elizabeth Ann Whitmer, sister of David Whitmer, in 1832. He works closely with Joseph Smith, David Whitmer, Martin Harris, John Whitmer, Sidney Rigdon, and William W. Phelps.

sources.title: Oliver Cowdery, Joseph Smith Papers biography

oliver-granger.name: Oliver Granger
oliver-granger.role: Church agent who settled Joseph Smith’s Kirtland debts
oliver-granger.dateNote: Section 117 names him at Far West on 8 July 1838, and he died at Kirtland in August 1841.
oliver-granger.importance: When Church leaders left Kirtland in 1838, debts and business affairs remained. Section 117 says his name will be held in “sacred remembrance” and tells him to work for the redemption of the First Presidency. It adds that when he falls he will rise again, because his sacrifice matters more than his increase. He returned to Kirtland to settle Joseph Smith’s business and later presided over the Church there.
oliver-granger.connections: Husband of Lydia Dibble. Section 117 names him with William Marks and Newel K. Whitney, who were told to leave Kirtland.

sources.title: Oliver Granger, Joseph Smith Papers

orson-hyde.name: Orson Hyde
orson-hyde.role: Early missionary, high councilor, and apostle
orson-hyde.dateNote: He was baptized in October 1831 and ordained one of the first Twelve Apostles on 15 February 1835.
orson-hyde.importance: Section 68 opens with his call to preach, given at Hiram in November 1831. Sections 75 and 103 send him on missions, and section 100 says he and John Gould are in the Lord’s hands. He was clerk of the first high council, whose minutes became section 102. He sided with dissenters in 1838 but was restored in 1839, and section 124 lists him among the Twelve.
orson-hyde.connections: Husband of Marinda Nancy Johnson until 1870. He served with Samuel H. Smith, Orson Pratt, Heber C. Kimball, and Thomas B. Marsh.

sources.title: Orson Hyde, Joseph Smith Papers

orson-pratt.name: Orson Pratt
orson-pratt.role: Missionary and member of the Quorum of the Twelve
orson-pratt.dateNote: Section 34 came on 4 November 1830, weeks after his baptism on his nineteenth birthday.
orson-pratt.importance: Section 34 calls the young convert Orson Pratt to preach and prophesy. Later revelations send him to Missouri in 1831, to the eastern states in 1832, and out to recruit for Zion in 1834. He became one of the first Twelve Apostles in 1835, was excommunicated in 1842, and was restored in 1843. Section 136 assigns him to organize a company for the trek west in 1847.
orson-pratt.connections: He was baptized by his older brother Parley P. Pratt, and section 52 sends the brothers together. Other companions named with him include Lyman Johnson, Orson Hyde, and Wilford Woodruff.

sources.title: Orson Pratt, Joseph Smith Papers biography

parley-p-pratt.name: Parley P. Pratt
parley-p-pratt.dateNote: He was baptized on 1 September 1830, ordained an apostle on 21 February 1835, and killed in Arkansas in 1857.
parley-p-pratt.importance: Section 32 sends him with Oliver Cowdery on the 1830–1831 mission to the Lamanites. Later revelations send him to the Shakers with Sidney Rigdon (49) and to strengthen the churches (50). In Missouri he led the school in Zion approved in section 97. In 1834 he brought news of the Jackson County expulsion to Kirtland, which led to section 103.
parley-p-pratt.connections: He was the older brother of Orson Pratt, whom he baptized. His companions in these sections include Oliver Cowdery, Ziba Peterson, Sidney Rigdon, Joseph Wakefield, and Lyman Wight.

sources.title: Parley Parker Pratt, Joseph Smith Papers biography

peter-haws.name: Peter Haws
peter-haws.dateNote: Section 124 named him to the Nauvoo House committee in January 1841.
peter-haws.importance: Section 124 names him with George Miller, Lyman Wight, and John Snider to organize and build the Nauvoo House. It tells them how to handle the stock they receive. In 1843 he and Amasa Lyman raised funds for the temple and the Nauvoo House. He later moved to Council Bluffs and was excommunicated in 1849.
peter-haws.connections: Husband of Charlotte Harrington. He worked with George Miller and visited Lyman Wight’s Texas colony in 1848.

sources.title: Peter Haws, Joseph Smith Papers
Peter Haws, Doctrine and Covenants Historical Resources

peter-james-john.name: Peter, James, and John
peter-james-john.role: Ancient apostles who restore priesthood keys in the D&C
peter-james-john.dateNote: Section 27, dated August 1830, says they had already ordained Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery apostles.
peter-james-john.importance: Peter, James, and John were apostles of Jesus in the New Testament. Section 7 presents a record of John’s wish to remain on earth and gives the three keys of ministry. Section 27 says the Lord sent them to ordain Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery apostles and gave them the keys of the kingdom. Section 128 places their voice between Harmony and Colesville on the Susquehanna River, without giving a date.
peter-james-john.connections: They appear with Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery, and alongside John the Baptist, who section 27 says conferred the lesser priesthood.

sources.title: Doctrine and Covenants 27

peter-whitmer-jr.name: Peter Whitmer Jr.
peter-whitmer-jr.role: Eight Witness and missionary to the Lamanites
peter-whitmer-jr.dateNote: He was baptized in Seneca Lake in June 1829 and left on the western mission in October 1830.
peter-whitmer-jr.importance: A young tailor on his father’s Fayette farm, he asked his duty while the translation was finished there. Section 16 answers him in the same words as section 15 to his brother John. He was one of the Eight Witnesses and one of six original members in April 1830. Sections 30 and 32 send him with Oliver Cowdery to preach to the Lamanites on the Missouri border.
peter-whitmer-jr.connections: Son of Peter Whitmer Sr. and Mary Musselman, and brother of David and John Whitmer. He married Vashti Higley in 1832 and died near Liberty, Missouri.

sources.title: Peter Whitmer Jr., Joseph Smith Papers

peter-whitmer-sr.name: Peter Whitmer Sr.
peter-whitmer-sr.role: Fayette farmer whose home hosted the Church’s founding
peter-whitmer-sr.dateNote: Translation was finished at his home in June 1829, and the Church was organized there on 6 April 1830.
peter-whitmer-sr.importance: Peter Whitmer Sr. owned the farm in Fayette, New York, where Joseph Smith finished translating in June 1829. The Church was organized at his home on 6 April 1830, and several early revelations were received there. Section 128 recalls “the voice of God in the chamber of old Father Whitmer.” He moved to Ohio and Missouri, became disaffected, and died in Richmond, Missouri.
peter-whitmer-sr.connections: He was the father of David, John, Christian, and Peter Whitmer Jr., and of Elizabeth Ann, who married Oliver Cowdery. His wife was Mary Musselman.

sources.title: Peter Whitmer Sr., Joseph Smith Papers biography

philip-burroughs.name: Philip Burroughs
philip-burroughs.role: Seneca County farmer whose home hosted early preaching
philip-burroughs.dateNote: Section 30, from September 1830, sends John Whitmer to preach at his home.
philip-burroughs.importance: Section 30 tells John Whitmer that his labor will be at Philip Burroughs’s home and the region around it. Church meetings were held in his home near Fayette that autumn. There is no record that he joined the Church himself.
philip-burroughs.connections: His wife, Anna Parker, was baptized. The revelation calls him John Whitmer’s “brother,” probably as a fellow believer or friend rather than a relative.

sources.title: Philip Burroughs, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reynolds-cahoon.name: Reynolds Cahoon
reynolds-cahoon.role: Missionary and temple building committee member
reynolds-cahoon.dateNote: He was baptized in November 1830 and joined the Kirtland temple building committee in June 1833.
reynolds-cahoon.importance: Section 52 sends him to Missouri with Samuel H. Smith, and section 61 tells the two to stay together. Section 75 pairs him with Hyrum Smith. Section 94 names him with Hyrum Smith and Jared Carter to build the Lord’s houses in Kirtland. He later served on the Nauvoo Temple building committee.
reynolds-cahoon.connections: He married Thirza Stiles in 1810. He worked with Hyrum Smith and Jared Carter and served as counselor to Bishop Newel K. Whitney.

sources.title: Reynolds Cahoon, Joseph Smith Papers biography

robert-b-thompson.name: Robert B. Thompson
robert-b-thompson.role: Church clerk and scribe in Nauvoo
robert-b-thompson.dateNote: Section 124, dated 19 January 1841, praises him; he died in Nauvoo that August.
robert-b-thompson.importance: Robert B. Thompson was an English Methodist who joined in Upper Canada in 1836. As Church clerk in 1840–41, he copied section 124 into the Book of the Law of the Lord. That revelation tells him to help write a proclamation to the rulers of the earth. He became associate editor of the Times and Seasons and died on 27 August 1841.
robert-b-thompson.connections: He married Mercy Rachel Fielding in 1837, making him a brother-in-law of Hyrum Smith.

sources.title: Robert Blashel Thompson, Joseph Smith Papers biography

robert-d-foster.name: Robert D. Foster
robert-d-foster.role: Nauvoo physician, later a publisher of the Nauvoo Expositor
robert-d-foster.dateNote: Section 124 named him on 19 January 1841; he was excommunicated on 18 April 1844.
robert-d-foster.importance: Robert D. Foster was an English-born doctor who joined by 1839 and travelled with Joseph Smith to Washington in 1839–40. Section 124 tells him to build a house for Joseph as contracted, repent of “his folly,” and buy Nauvoo House stock. In 1844 he broke with Joseph Smith and was excommunicated. He then became a publisher of the Nauvoo Expositor, whose destruction led to Joseph’s arrest.
robert-d-foster.connections: Section 124 tells him to heed Joseph Smith, Hyrum Smith, and William Law. He later joined Law’s breakaway church.

sources.title: Robert D. Foster, Joseph Smith Papers biography
Robert D. Foster, Wikipedia

ruggles-eames.name: Ruggles Eames
ruggles-eames.role: Early Ohio priest called to preach
ruggles-eames.dateNote: He was ordained a priest on 25 October 1831 and called to preach by section 75 on 25 January 1832.
ruggles-eames.importance: Section 75 pairs him with Stephen Burnett to preach. Little is known of his service. He bought property in Caldwell County, Missouri, by 1839 and lived in Iowa Territory by 1840.
ruggles-eames.connections: Son of Benjamin Eames and Julia Bacon, and husband of Charlotte Rose. Called with Stephen Burnett.

sources.title: Ruggles Eames, Joseph Smith Papers

samuel-smith.name: Samuel H. Smith
samuel-smith.role: Joseph Smith’s brother and early missionary
samuel-smith.dateNote: He was baptized in May 1829 and died at Nauvoo on 30 July 1844, about a month after his brothers Joseph and Hyrum.
samuel-smith.importance: Section 23 calls him to exhort and strengthen the Church in April 1830. Later revelations send him to Missouri with Reynolds Cahoon (52, 61) and east with Orson Hyde (66, 75). He sat on the first Kirtland high council in February 1834 (102). Section 124 names him with Vinson Knight to preside over a bishopric at Nauvoo.
samuel-smith.connections: He was a younger brother of Joseph and Hyrum Smith and a son of Joseph Smith Sr. and Lucy Mack Smith. His missionary companions in these sections were Reynolds Cahoon, William E. McLellin, and Orson Hyde.

sources.title: Samuel Harrison Smith, Joseph Smith Papers biography

selah-griffin.name: Selah J. Griffin
selah-griffin.role: Early Kirtland elder sent to Missouri
selah-griffin.dateNote: He was ordained an elder on 6 June 1831, the day section 52 named him.
selah-griffin.importance: Section 52 tells him to be ordained and travel to Missouri with Newel Knight. Section 56 cancels that pairing because of rebellion among the Saints at Thompson. It sends him with Thomas B. Marsh instead. He settled in Jackson County and later served in the Seventy.
selah-griffin.connections: His named companions are Newel Knight and Thomas B. Marsh.

sources.title: Selah J. Griffin, Joseph Smith Papers biography

seymour-brunson.name: Seymour Brunson
seymour-brunson.role: Early elder and member of the Nauvoo high council
seymour-brunson.dateNote: He was baptized in January 1831, called to preach by section 75 in 1832, and died at Nauvoo on 10 August 1840.
seymour-brunson.importance: Section 75 pairs him with Daniel Stanton for preaching in 1832. He later moved to Missouri and joined the Nauvoo high council in 1839. At his funeral on 15 August 1840, Joseph Smith first taught publicly that the living could be baptized for the dead. Section 124 lists him on the high council with the note “I have taken unto myself.”
seymour-brunson.connections: Baptized by Solomon Hancock. Section 124 names Aaron Johnson to take his place on the high council.

sources.title: Seymour Brunson, Joseph Smith Papers
Baptism for the Dead, Church History Topics

sidney-gilbert.name: Algernon Sidney Gilbert
sidney-gilbert.role: Church agent and storekeeper in Zion
sidney-gilbert.dateNote: He was baptized in spring 1831, went to Missouri in June 1831, and died of cholera in Clay County, Missouri, on 29 June 1834.
sidney-gilbert.importance: Section 53 answers his prayer about his calling in June 1831. Section 57 makes him the Church’s agent in Zion, to buy land and open a store. He joined the United Firm (78, 82). After the Jackson County expulsion, section 101 tells him not to sell the storehouse.
sidney-gilbert.connections: He was the business partner of Newel K. Whitney in Kirtland. He worked with Edward Partridge and William W. Phelps in Missouri.

sources.title: Algernon Sidney Gilbert, Joseph Smith Papers biography

sidney-rigdon.name: Sidney Rigdon
sidney-rigdon.role: Counselor to Joseph Smith in the First Presidency
sidney-rigdon.dateNote: He was baptized in November 1830 and shared the vision in section 76 on 16 February 1832.
sidney-rigdon.importance: Sidney Rigdon was a Reformed Baptist preacher in Ohio when he joined in November 1830. Section 35 calls him to be Joseph Smith’s scribe, and section 76 reports that the two saw the vision of the degrees of glory together. He served as counselor in the presidency from 1832 and was jailed with Joseph in Missouri. After Joseph’s death he claimed the right to lead and was excommunicated in 1844.
sidney-rigdon.connections: Parley P. Pratt introduced him to the Church and Oliver Cowdery baptized him. He travels with Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery in many sections, and section 100 makes him Joseph’s spokesman.

sources.title: Sidney Rigdon, Joseph Smith Papers biography
Sidney Rigdon, Wikipedia

simeon-carter.name: Simeon Carter
simeon-carter.role: Early Ohio missionary and Missouri high councilor
simeon-carter.dateNote: He was baptized in February 1831 and ordained a high priest at the June 1831 conference.
simeon-carter.importance: Section 52 sends him to Missouri with Solomon Hancock in June 1831. Section 75 pairs him with Emer Harris for further preaching in 1832. He presided over a branch on the Big Blue River in Jackson County before the 1833 expulsion. He later sat on the Missouri high council and served a mission to England.
simeon-carter.connections: Son of Gideon Carter and Johanna Sims. He was the oldest of the Carter brothers named in the D&C, including Jared, Gideon, and John S. Carter.

sources.title: Simeon Carter, Joseph Smith Papers
Simeon Carter, Doctrine and Covenants Central

simonds-ryder.name: Simonds Ryder
simonds-ryder.role: Hiram preacher who joined briefly, then opposed the Church
simonds-ryder.dateNote: He was ordained an elder on 6 June 1831 and had left the Church by September 1831.
simonds-ryder.importance: Section 52 transfers to him the office taken from Heman Basset because of transgression. Ryder left within months and returned to leading the Disciples congregation at Hiram. Later accounts say a misspelling of his name in his commission troubled him, along with fears about consecration. Joseph Smith’s history names him among the mob that tarred and feathered Joseph at Hiram in March 1832.
simonds-ryder.connections: He had been a Disciples (Campbellite) leader at Hiram before joining. His case is tied to Heman Basset and to the Johnson family of Hiram.

sources.title: Symonds (Simonds) Rider (Ryder), Joseph Smith Papers
Symonds Ryder, Doctrine and Covenants Central

stephen-burnett.name: Stephen Burnett
stephen-burnett.role: Young Ohio elder called on missions in 1832
stephen-burnett.dateNote: Section 75 named him in January 1832, and section 80 was given to him on 7 March 1832, at age eighteen.
stephen-burnett.importance: Stephen Burnett was baptized in Ohio in November 1830 and ordained a high priest in October 1831. Section 75 pairs him with Ruggles Eames, and section 80 tells him to preach with Eden Smith as companion. He served in New Hampshire and other eastern states from 1832 to 1834. He left the Church by 1838 and later became a Disciples of Christ elder.
stephen-burnett.connections: His named companions are Ruggles Eames (75:35) and Eden Smith (80:2).

sources.title: Stephen Burnett, Joseph Smith Papers biography

sylvester-smith.name: Sylvester Smith
sylvester-smith.role: Early elder, high councilor, and Seventy president
sylvester-smith.dateNote: Section 75 named him in January 1832, and section 102 lists him on the high council in February 1834.
sylvester-smith.importance: Sylvester Smith lived at Amherst, Ohio, and joined by June 1831; section 75 pairs him with Gideon Carter for a mission. Section 102 lists him on the first Kirtland high council. During the 1834 march to Missouri he clashed with Joseph Smith, and later confessed to false charges. He became a president of the Seventy in 1835 and had left the Church by 1838.
sylvester-smith.connections: His named companion is Gideon Carter (75:34). He served on the high council with Oliver Cowdery, Joseph Coe, and others.

sources.title: Sylvester Smith, Joseph Smith Papers biography

thomas-b-marsh.name: Thomas B. Marsh
thomas-b-marsh.role: First president of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
thomas-b-marsh.dateNote: He was baptized on 3 September 1830, ordained an apostle in April 1835, and left the Church in October 1838.
thomas-b-marsh.importance: Section 31 was given for him in September 1830, soon after his baptism. Sections 52, 56, and 75 send him on missions, first with Ezra Thayre. As president of the Twelve he received section 112 in 1837, which names him to hold the keys for the Twelve abroad. Section 118 tells him to stay in Missouri to publish, but he left the Church that October.
thomas-b-marsh.connections: He was paired with Ezra Thayre and later Selah J. Griffin for missions. Orson Hyde signed a Richmond affidavit with him in October 1838.

sources.title: Thomas Baldwin Marsh, Joseph Smith Papers

titus-billings.name: Titus Billings
