titus-billings.role: Caretaker of the Morley farm and later bishop’s counselor
titus-billings.dateNote: He was baptized on 15 November 1830, and section 63 told him in August 1831 to sell the farm and move to Zion.
titus-billings.importance: Section 63 says he “has the care” of the Kirtland farm where many Saints lived. It tells him to dispose of the land and lead its residents to Missouri the next spring. He was ordained an elder in March 1832 while on the way to Jackson County. He later served as a counselor to Bishop Edward Partridge in Missouri and Illinois.
titus-billings.connections: Husband of Diantha Morley, the younger sister of Isaac Morley, whose farm he managed. He worked under Bishop Edward Partridge.

sources.title: Titus Billings, Joseph Smith Papers
Titus Billings, Wikipedia

vienna-jaques.name: Vienna Jaques
vienna-jaques.role: Boston convert who consecrated her savings to the Church
vienna-jaques.dateNote: Section 90, dated 8 March 1833, directs her to go to Zion; she reached Missouri by July 1833.
vienna-jaques.importance: Vienna Jaques was a laundress and nurse from Boston, baptized in July 1831, who moved to Kirtland and gave her money to the Church. Section 90 says she should receive money for her journey and an inheritance in Zion. She reached Independence in 1833 and nursed the sick in the 1834 camp. She later lived in Nauvoo and crossed the plains in 1847.
vienna-jaques.connections: Section 90 calls her “my handmaid” and says she should settle “in peace” on an inheritance from the bishop. She married Daniel Shearer about 1839.

sources.title: Vienna Jaques, Joseph Smith Papers biography

vinson-knight.name: Vinson Knight
vinson-knight.role: Bishop at Kirtland, Missouri, and Nauvoo
vinson-knight.dateNote: He was baptized in spring 1834 and became a bishop at Commerce in 1839; section 124 dates from January 1841.
vinson-knight.importance: He served as counselor to Bishop Newel K. Whitney in Kirtland and as acting bishop at Adam-ondi-Ahman. In Illinois he helped buy land for the Saints and became a bishop at Commerce. Section 124 invites him to put stock into the Nauvoo House. It also names him with Samuel H. Smith and Shadrach Roundy to preside over a bishopric.
vinson-knight.connections: He married Martha McBride in 1826. He worked under Newel K. Whitney and with Samuel H. Smith.

sources.title: Vinson Knight, Joseph Smith Papers biography

warren-cowdery.name: Warren A. Cowdery
warren-cowdery.role: Presiding high priest at Freedom and Kirtland clerk
warren-cowdery.dateNote: He was baptized in 1834 and called to preside at Freedom on 25 November 1834; he recorded the 3 April 1836 visions.
warren-cowdery.importance: Section 106 calls him to preside over the Church in Freedom, New York, and nearby areas. It also warns him about the vanity of his heart. After moving to Kirtland he worked as an editor and clerk. He wrote the account of the 3 April 1836 temple visions in Joseph Smith’s journal, which became section 110.
warren-cowdery.connections: He was an older brother of Oliver Cowdery. He became disaffected from Church leaders in 1838.

sources.title: Warren A. Cowdery, Joseph Smith Papers biography

wilford-woodruff.name: Wilford Woodruff
wilford-woodruff.role: Apostle and later President of the Church
wilford-woodruff.dateNote: Section 118 named him to the Twelve on 8 July 1838; he was ordained at Far West on 26 April 1839.
wilford-woodruff.importance: Wilford Woodruff joined at the end of 1833, and section 118 names him to fill a vacancy in the Twelve in 1838. He served in Britain from 1839 to 1841, and section 124 lists him among the apostles. Section 136 assigns him with Orson Pratt to organize a company in 1847. He presided over the Church from 1889 to 1898, and section 138 sees him among the spirits of the dead.
wilford-woodruff.connections: He married Phebe Carter in 1837. Section 118 names him with John Taylor, John E. Page, and Willard Richards.

sources.title: Wilford Woodruff, Joseph Smith Papers biography

willard-richards.name: Willard Richards
willard-richards.role: Apostle, Church historian, and survivor of Carthage Jail
willard-richards.dateNote: He was called as an apostle by section 118 in July 1838 and ordained in England on 14 April 1840.
willard-richards.importance: Section 118 names him to fill a vacancy in the Twelve while he was serving in England. He became Joseph Smith’s secretary and Church historian in 1842 and recorded his teachings. His records lie behind sections 110, 126, 129, and 130. Section 135 says he and John Taylor were the only others in the Carthage jail room in 1844, and he escaped unhurt.
willard-richards.connections: Baptized by Brigham Young and later Young’s counselor in the First Presidency. He married Jennetta Richards in England in 1838.

sources.title: Willard Richards, Joseph Smith Papers

william-law.name: William Law
william-law.role: Counselor in the First Presidency who became a leading dissenter
william-law.dateNote: Section 124 named him a counselor in January 1841, and he was excommunicated on 18 April 1844.
william-law.importance: Section 124 names him to the First Presidency, tells him to invest in the Nauvoo House, and promises him spiritual gifts if he stays humble. By 1844 he opposed Joseph Smith over the secret practice of plural marriage and other matters. He formed a rival church and published the Nauvoo Expositor in June 1844. The city council ordered the press destroyed, and the resulting charges took Joseph Smith to Carthage.
william-law.connections: He served with Joseph Smith, Hyrum Smith, and Sidney Rigdon. Law said Joseph had approached his wife, Jane, a claim Joseph’s supporters denied.

sources.title: William Law, Joseph Smith Papers
William Law (Latter Day Saints), Wikipedia

william-marks.name: William Marks
william-marks.role: Stake president at Kirtland and Nauvoo
william-marks.dateNote: Section 117 called him to Far West on 8 July 1838; he became Nauvoo stake president on 5 October 1839.
william-marks.importance: William Marks presided over the Church in Kirtland in 1838. Section 117 tells him to settle his business and preside at Far West, but the Missouri conflict stopped that plan. In 1839 he became stake president at Commerce, later Nauvoo, and section 124 asks him to buy Nauvoo House stock and ordain Isaac Galland. After Joseph Smith’s death he backed Sidney Rigdon and James Strang, and in 1859 joined the Reorganized Church.
william-marks.connections: Section 117 pairs him with Bishop Newel K. Whitney, and section 124 links him with Isaac Galland and Hyrum Smith.

sources.title: William Marks, Joseph Smith Papers biography

william-mclellin.name: William E. McLellin
william-mclellin.role: Early missionary and apostle who later left the Church
william-mclellin.dateNote: He was baptized in August 1831 and met Joseph Smith that October; he became an apostle in 1835 and was excommunicated in 1838.
william-mclellin.importance: Section 66 answers five questions he had asked privately, and he wrote that it answered them fully. Joseph Smith’s history says that soon after, he tried to write a revelation and failed (67). Section 68 sends him to preach, and section 75 revokes his eastern mission and rebukes him for murmuring. He later recalled how the preface (section 1) was produced.
william-mclellin.connections: His missionary companions in these sections were Samuel H. Smith and Luke Johnson. He was called to the Twelve with Lyman Johnson, Orson Hyde, and others in 1835.

sources.title: William E. McLellin, Joseph Smith Papers biography

william-w-phelps.name: William W. Phelps
william-w-phelps.role: Church printer and editor in Missouri
william-w-phelps.dateNote: He was baptized on 16 June 1831, two days after section 55, and was named Church printer in July 1831.
william-w-phelps.importance: William W. Phelps was a newspaper editor from Canandaigua, New York. Section 55 calls him to be baptized and to help Oliver Cowdery with printing and school books. Section 57 plants him at Independence as Church printer, where a mob destroyed his press on 20 July 1833. He helped compile the 1835 D&C and its hymnal; he was excommunicated in 1838 and 1839 and rebaptized in 1840.
william-w-phelps.connections: He works with Oliver Cowdery, John Whitmer, and Martin Harris on the revelations, and served as counselor to David Whitmer in Missouri.

sources.title: William Wines Phelps, Joseph Smith Papers biography

zebedee-coltrin.name: Zebedee Coltrin
zebedee-coltrin.role: Early elder and president of the Seventy
zebedee-coltrin.dateNote: Section 52 sent him to Missouri on 6 June 1831; he became a Seventy president in February 1835.
zebedee-coltrin.importance: Zebedee Coltrin was baptized in Ohio in January 1831, and section 52 sends him to Missouri with Levi W. Hancock. He attended the School of the Prophets in 1833 and marched with the 1834 camp to Missouri. In 1835 he became one of the presidents of the Seventy. He went west with the 1847 pioneer company and died at Spanish Fork, Utah.
zebedee-coltrin.connections: Section 52 pairs him with Levi W. Hancock; in 1832 he travelled briefly with Jesse Gause.

sources.title: Zebedee Coltrin, Joseph Smith Papers biography
Zebedee Coltrin, Wikipedia

ziba-peterson.name: Ziba Peterson
ziba-peterson.role: Early elder on the 1830 mission to the Lamanites
ziba-peterson.dateNote: He was an elder by June 1830 and was named for the western mission in October 1830.
ziba-peterson.importance: Section 32 adds him to the mission of Oliver Cowdery, Peter Whitmer Jr., and Parley P. Pratt to the Lamanites. In August 1831 section 58 takes away what had been given him, because he had not confessed his sins. He was reordained in 1832 but was excommunicated by June 1833. He later moved to California and served as a sheriff.
ziba-peterson.connections: He traveled with Oliver Cowdery, Parley P. Pratt, and Peter Whitmer Jr. He married Rebecca Hopper in Missouri in August 1831.

sources.title: Ziba Peterson, Joseph Smith Papers
